claim: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is a biflagellated fresh water green alga.
source: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is uniquely suited for addressing these issues. The unicellular fresh water green alga has signature features of both animal and plant cells (Merchant et al., 2007).
evidence: Stated directly in the text with citation support

claim: Chlamydomonas has signature features of both animal and plant cells.
source: The unicellular fresh water green alga has signature features of both animal and plant cells (Merchant et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Merchant et al., 2007

claim: Chlamydomonas has motile flagella that contain stable MT bundles like animal cells.
source: Like animal cells, it has motile flagella that contain stable MT bundles.

claim: Chlamydomonas is equipped with vacuoles, chloroplast, and dynamic cortical MTs like typical plant cells.
source: Like typical plant cells, the alga is equipped with vacuoles, chloroplast, and dynamic cortical MTs that serve as tracks for the delivery of the enzymes which synthesize the cell wall (Paredez et al., 2006).

claim: Dynamic cortical MTs in Chlamydomonas serve as tracks for the delivery of enzymes which synthesize the cell wall.
source: Like typical plant cells, the alga is equipped with vacuoles, chloroplast, and dynamic cortical MTs that serve as tracks for the delivery of the enzymes which synthesize the cell wall (Paredez et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Paredez et al., 2006

claim: Chlamydomonas flagella sever readily when the aqueous environment changes suddenly.
source: Curiously, its MT system appears susceptible to environmental changes. Its flagella sever readily when the aqueous environment changes suddenly (Lefebvre et al., 1978); reviewed by Quarmby, 2009).

claim: pH shock is the best characterized stimulus for flagellar severing in Chlamydomonas.
source: The best characterized stimulus is pH shock.

claim: Organic acid such as acetic acid diffuses across the plasma membrane and then becomes ionized.
source: Organic acid, such as acetic acid (HA) diffuses across the plasma membrane and then becomes ionized.
evidence: Direct statement based on chemical properties

claim: Acidification in the cytosol triggers nearly simultaneous influx of extracellular Ca2+, which signals flagella amputation.
source: The resulting acidification in the cytosol triggers nearly simultaneous influx of extracellular Ca2+, which signals flagella amputation (Quarmby, 1996; Wheeler et al., 2008; Hilton et al., 2016).

claim: Cortical MTs become fewer and shorter 5 min after pH shock, detected by immunofluorescence and biochemistry.
source: Cortical MTs become fewer and shorter, detected by immunofluorescence and biochemistry 5 min after pH shock (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2013

claim: Autofluorescence from photosynthetic pigments in chloroplast obscures commonly used fluorescent reporters in Chlamydomonas.
source: While live cell imaging will be ideal for revealing these acid-induced responses with higher spatial and temporal resolution, autofluorescence from photosynthetic pigments in chloroplast obscures commonly used fluorescent reporters (Lang et al., 1991; Rasala et al., 2013).

claim: NeonGreen (NG) is 2.7 X brighter than EGFP.
source: Recently, we succeeded in revealing dynamic cortical MTs by taking advantage of the new fluorescent protein, NeonGreen (NG) that is 2.7 X brighter than EGFP (Shaner et al., 2013), and the relative abundant plus end-binding protein, EB1, as the NG carrier (Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shaner et al., 2013

claim: EB1 plays central roles in eukaryotes.
source: EB1 plays central roles in eukaryotes (Su et al., 1995; reviewed by Akhmanova and Steinmetz, 2010; Kumar and Wittmann, 2012).

claim: EB1's N-terminal domain preferentially binds to the lattice among tubulins at the plus end of MTs.
source: Its N-terminal domain preferentially binds to the lattice among tubulins at the plus end of MTs, whereas its C-terminal domain can associate with a wide array of proteins.

claim: EB1's C-terminal domain can associate with a wide array of proteins.
source: Its N-terminal domain preferentially binds to the lattice among tubulins at the plus end of MTs, whereas its C-terminal domain can associate with a wide array of proteins.

claim: EB1's two domains operate in concert to accelerate MT dynamics.
source: The two domains operate in concert to accelerate MT dynamics (Rogers et al., 2002; Vitre et al., 2008; Maurer et al., 2014) and recruit various+ TIP effector proteins that function at the plus end.

claim: EB1's two domains recruit various +TIP effector proteins that function at the plus end.
source: The two domains operate in concert to accelerate MT dynamics (Rogers et al., 2002; Vitre et al., 2008; Maurer et al., 2014) and recruit various+ TIP effector proteins that function at the plus end.

claim: Fluorescent EB1 exhibits a comet pattern in live cell imaging.
source: In live cell imaging, fluorescent EB1 exhibits a comet pattern seemingly leading the plus end of nascent growing MTs, where tubulins transition from the GTP state to the GDP state (Maurer et al., 2012; Zanic et al., 2009; reviewed by Gardner et al., 2013).

claim: Fluorescent EB1 has been commonly used to report newly generated growing MTs.
source: As such fluorescent EB1 has been commonly used to report newly generated growing MTs (Piehl et al., 2004; Matov et al., 2010).

claim: EB1 binding to the GDP zone increases in a number of scenarios.
source: However, binding to the GDP zone increases in a number of scenarios (e.g. Tirnauer et al., 2002; Goldspink et al., 2013; Tortosa et al., 2013; Sayas and Ávila, 2014).

claim: Flagellated Chlamydomonas cells in interphase contain two mature basal bodies and two probasal bodies.
source: Flagellated Chlamydomonas cells in interphase contain two mature basal bodies (BBs) and two probasal bodies (Figure 1a, top panel) that are templated on mature BBs.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1a

claim: Probasal bodies are templated on mature BBs.
source: Flagellated Chlamydomonas cells in interphase contain two mature basal bodies (BBs) and two probasal bodies (Figure 1a, top panel) that are templated on mature BBs.

claim: Each mature BB nucleates the assembly of the axoneme.
source: Each of mature BBs that are derived from centrioles following cell division nucleates the assembly of the axoneme, a MT-based scaffold that drives the rhythmic beating of the flagellum (Dutcher and O'Toole, 2016).

claim: The axoneme is a MT-based scaffold that drives the rhythmic beating of the flagellum.
source: Each of mature BBs that are derived from centrioles following cell division nucleates the assembly of the axoneme, a MT-based scaffold that drives the rhythmic beating of the flagellum (Dutcher and O'Toole, 2016).

claim: Four rootlet MT bundles arrange in a cruciate pattern positioning BBs at the apical end and the other organelles.
source: Four rootlet MT bundles (thick lines) arrange in a cruciate pattern positioning BBs at the apical end and the other organelles (Mittelmeier et al., 2011; Picariello et al., 2014).

claim: Rootlet MT bundles consist of more than two acetylated stable MTs.
source: These MT bundles consisting of more than two acetylated stable MTs.

claim: Cortical MTs in Chlamydomonas are singular.
source: In contrast, cortical MTs (thin lines) are singular (Horst et al., 1999) and highly dynamic (Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Horst et al., 1999

claim: Cortical MTs in Chlamydomonas are highly dynamic.
source: In contrast, cortical MTs (thin lines) are singular (Horst et al., 1999) and highly dynamic (Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harris et al., 2016

claim: EB1-NG expressed at the level of endogenous EB1 does not reveal stable MTs under widefield fluorescence microscopy except the flagellar tip.
source: Under widefield fluorescence microscopy EB1-NG expressed at the level of endogenous EB1 from a genomic construct does not reveal stable MTs except the flagellar tip where plus ends of axonemal MTs undergo turnover continuously (Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harris et al., 2016

claim: Plus ends of axonemal MTs at the flagellar tip undergo turnover continuously.
source: Under widefield fluorescence microscopy EB1-NG expressed at the level of endogenous EB1 from a genomic construct does not reveal stable MTs except the flagellar tip where plus ends of axonemal MTs undergo turnover continuously (Harris et al., 2016).

claim: Plus ends of growing cortical MTs appear like typical comets observed in other eukaryotic cells.
source: In addition, plus ends of growing cortical MTs appear like the typical comets observed in other eukaryotic cells.

claim: Comets emerge from four spots underneath flagella, corresponding to BBs.
source: Comets emerged from four spots underneath flagella, corresponding to BBs (bottom panel) (Pedersen et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated in text with citation and shown in Figure 1a bottom panel

claim: Comets of nascent cortical MTs travel along the contour of the cell body toward the posterior pole.
source: As shown from the top, side and rear views of cells, comets of nascent cortical MTs travel along the contour of the cell body toward the posterior pole (Figure 1b, white arrowhead; Video 1).

claim: Near the pole comets vanish presumably when MTs stop growing or switch to the shrinking phase.
source: Near the pole comets vanish presumably when MTs stop growing or switch to the shrinking phase.

claim: The EB1-NG comet pattern appears similar in cells resuspended in TAP culture medium or 10 mM HEPES buffer.
source: The pattern appears similar in cells resuspended in the commonly used Tris Acetate Phosphate (TAP) culture medium or 10 mM HEPES buffer (containing 5 mM Na+).

claim: Line scans along the lengths of comets show the typical feature of EB1 comets - the brightest spot corresponds to the area where tubulins are primarily at the transitional state, slightly behind the leading edge of plus ends with GTP-tubulins.
source: Line scans along the lengths of comets show the typical feature of EB1 comets - the brightest spot corresponds to the area where tubulins are primarily at the transitional state, slightly behind the leading edge of plus ends with GTP-tubulins (Figure 1c).

claim: MT growth rates vary nearly two folds.
source: The distribution of comet speeds shows that MT growth rates varies nearly two folds (Figure 1d).

claim: The dataset from cells in the TAP medium skews toward the slow end relative to the Na+/HEPES dataset.
source: The dataset from cells in the TAP medium (black bars) skews toward the slow end relative to the Na+/HEPES dataset (hatched bars).

claim: The average velocities of EB1 comets in TAP medium and Na+/HEPES are significantly different (Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.001), at 5.8 ± 0.26 and 7.9 ± 0.42 μm/sec respectively.
source: The average velocities are signifantly different (Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.001), at 5.8 ± 0.26 and 7.9 ± 0.42 μm/sec respectively (Figure 1e), which are within the normal range measured in diverse eukaryotic cells (Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: Statistical analysis shown in Figure 1e with citation

claim: The measured MT growth rates are within the normal range measured in diverse eukaryotic cells.
source: The average velocities are signifantly different (Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.001), at 5.8 ± 0.26 and 7.9 ± 0.42 μm/sec respectively (Figure 1e), which are within the normal range measured in diverse eukaryotic cells (Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harris et al., 2016

claim: In some long recordings, comets suddenly gave way to a bird cage-like pattern as if all cortical MTs were revealed by anti-tubulin immunofluorescence.
source: Curiously, in some long recordings, comets suddenly gave way to a bird cage-like pattern (Figure 1f1, top panel; Video 2 ) as if all cortical MTs were revealed by anti-tubulin immunofluorescence (Horst et al., 1999; Dymek et al., 2006).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1f1 and Video 2 with citations

claim: Comets returned automatically after ~1 min from the bird cage pattern.
source: Comets returned automatically after ~1 min (middle and bottom panels).

claim: The unpredictability of the bird cage pattern suggests that this pattern is caused by fluctuated intracellular conditions.
source: This unpredictability suggests that this pattern is caused by fluctuated intracellular conditions.

claim: When cells gradually flattened by the coverslip, MTs became visible as a broken bird cage with comets.
source: When cells gradually flattened by the coverslip, MTs also became visible as a broken bird cage with comets (Figure 1f2, top panel, t1; Video 3).

claim: Comets disappeared after ~100 s in flattened cells under illumination.
source: However, comets disappeared after ~100 s (bottom panel, t2).

claim: After a 30 s dark period, comets returned upon excitation light was switched back.
source: Interestingly, after a 30 s dark period, comets returned upon excitation light was switched back (t3).

claim: Simply alternating the dark and light period replicated the disappearance and return of comets.
source: Simply alternating the dark and light period replicated the disappearance and return of comets (t4 and t5).

claim: Excitation illumination creates a condition that is unfavorable for MT dynamics, but is reversed in the dark.
source: These observations demonstrate that Chlamydomonas MT system is sensitive to certain signals; and suggests that excitation illumination creates a condition that is unfavorable for MT dynamics, but is reversed in the dark.

claim: Illumination opens channelrhodopsins that conduct a number of cations and Cl-.
source: As illumination opens channelrhodopsins that conduct a number of cations and Cl- (Nagel et al., 2002; 2003); reviewed by Hegemann and Berthold, 2009), we hypothesize that changes of electrolyte concentrations modulate the MT system in Chlamydomonas.

claim: Changes of electrolyte concentrations modulate the MT system in Chlamydomonas.
source: As illumination opens channelrhodopsins that conduct a number of cations and Cl- (Nagel et al., 2002; 2003); reviewed by Hegemann and Berthold, 2009), we hypothesize that changes of electrolyte concentrations modulate the MT system in Chlamydomonas.

claim: Following the injection of 20 mM HA/TAP into the perfusion chamber, all comets vanished in the first discernable image taken at ~90 s.
source: Following the injection of 20 mM HA/TAP into the perfusion chamber, all comets vanished in the first discernable image taken at ~90 s (Figure 2, b1-b2).

claim: After wash with 10 mM pH7 HEPES, comets re-appeared at the BB area within ~45 s and MT dynamics resumed.
source: After wash with 10 mM pH7 HEPES, comets re-appeared at the BB area within ~45 s and MT dynamics resumed (b3-b5).

claim: HA exposure elicits the disappearance of EB patterns either by perturbing EB-MT interplays or causing cortical MTs to pause or disassemble.
source: Thus, HA exposure elicits the disappearance of EB patterns either by perturbing EB-MT interplays or causing cortical MTs to pause or disassemble.

claim: New dynamic MTs re-form rapidly after HA is washed away.
source: New dynamic MTs re-form rapidly after HA is washed away.

claim: A broken bird cage pattern with a few MTs and comets appeared before the disappearance at a time designated as 78 s in diffusion chambers.
source: A broken bird cage pattern with a few MTs (Figure 2c, left and middle panel, black arrowhead) and comets (white arrowheads) appeared before the disappearance at a time designated as 78 s (right panel).

claim: Some MTs clearly underwent endwise resorption during HA exposure.
source: As shown in two representative cells, overall EB1 signals were fading with time, which could be due to photobleaching, pH sensitivity of fluorescent proteins, disassociation of EB1 or system-wide MT disassembly. Some MTs clearly underwent endwise resorption (arrowheads).

claim: The initial shortening speeds for two tracked MTs are 8 and 13 μm/min but decelerate toward the BB area.
source: Measurements of the slopes show that the initial shortening speeds for these two events are 8 and 13 μm/min but decelerate toward the BB area.

claim: These shortening speeds revealed by EB1-NG are in line with the averaged 10 ± 3 μm/min shortening speed of cortical MTs in cultured tobacco cells.
source: These speeds revealed by EB1-NG are in line with the averaged 10 ± 3 μm/min shortening speed of cortical MTs in cultured tobacco cells (Dixit and Cyr, 2004), faster than kinesin-13 catalyzed shortening (Helenius et al., 2006), and slower than the maximal shortening speed (30 μm/min) of MTs assembled from purified tubulins (O'Brien et al., 1997).

claim: The measured shortening speeds are faster than kinesin-13 catalyzed shortening.
source: These speeds revealed by EB1-NG are in line with the averaged 10 ± 3 μm/min shortening speed of cortical MTs in cultured tobacco cells (Dixit and Cyr, 2004), faster than kinesin-13 catalyzed shortening (Helenius et al., 2006), and slower than the maximal shortening speed (30 μm/min) of MTs assembled from purified tubulins (O'Brien et al., 1997).

claim: The measured shortening speeds are slower than the maximal shortening speed (30 μm/min) of MTs assembled from purified tubulins.
source: These speeds revealed by EB1-NG are in line with the averaged 10 ± 3 μm/min shortening speed of cortical MTs in cultured tobacco cells (Dixit and Cyr, 2004), faster than kinesin-13 catalyzed shortening (Helenius et al., 2006), and slower than the maximal shortening speed (30 μm/min) of MTs assembled from purified tubulins (O'Brien et al., 1997).

claim: In cells with EB1 signals detected in the cell body and flagella simultaneously, comets vanished first before flagella were amputated.
source: As for cells with EB1 signals detected in the cell body and flagella (Figure 2e) simultaneously, comets (white arrowheads in left panel) vanished first (middle panel) before flagella (arrow) were amputated (right panel).

claim: EB1 signals remained at the BB area but were static after comets vanished.
source: EB1 signals remained at the BB area but were static (black arrowhead).

claim: Deflagellation in the diffusion chamber takes more than one minute due to gradual acidification, contrary to deflagellation within seconds upon HA perfusion.
source: Contrary to deflagellation within seconds upon HA perfusion (Wheeler et al., 2008), the deflagellation in the diffusion chamber takes more than one minute due to gradual acidification.
evidence: Comparison with cited data and experimental observation

claim: When cells are exposed to HA, shank binding increases, comets disappear, endwise resorption becomes evident and then flagella become amputated.
source: Thus, when cells are exposed to HA, shank binding increases, comets disappear, endwise resorption becomes evident and then flagella become amputated.

claim: These events do not require the contents unique to TAP media.
source: These events do not require the contents unique to TAP media.
evidence: Inference from experiments in different media

claim: Lowering intracellular pH elicits Ca2+ influx.
source: Lowering intracellular pH elicits Ca2+ influx, whereas Ca2+ prevents MT formation and promotes MT disassembly (Weisenberg, 1972; O'Brien et al., 1997).

claim: Ca2+ prevents MT formation and promotes MT disassembly.
source: Lowering intracellular pH elicits Ca2+ influx, whereas Ca2+ prevents MT formation and promotes MT disassembly (Weisenberg, 1972; O'Brien et al., 1997).

claim: WT cells resuspended in 30 mM Ca2+/HEPES appeared agitated, suggesting entry of Ca2+.
source: WT cells resuspended in 30 mM Ca2+/HEPES appeared agitated, suggesting entry of Ca2+ (Figure 2g, top panel).
evidence: Observation with inference shown in Figure 2g

claim: In 30 mM Ca2+/HEPES, flagella remained attached and comet activity was robust.
source: However, flagella remained attached (arrows) and comet activity was robust.

claim: When cells were resuspended in 75 mM Ca2+/HEPES solution, cells shed flagella and comets disappeared.
source: When cells were resuspended in 75 mM Ca2+/HEPES solution (right panel), cells shed flagella (arrows). Comets already disappeared, while static EB1 signals remained at the BB area (arrowhead).

claim: The outcomes elicited by high [Ca2+]ex and ≥ 20 mM HA are similar.
source: Thus, the outcomes elicited by high [Ca2+]ex and ≥ 20 mM HA are similar.

claim: All WT cells in 5 mM HA had motile flagella and had a dynamic bird cage pattern in which MTs shrink or grow with a comet.
source: As shown in two top view images taken 40 s apart immediately after resuspension in 5 mM HA (Figure 3a; Video 4), all WT cells had motile flagella and had a dynamic, rather than still, bird cage pattern in which MTs shrink or grow with a comet, as if the entire MT system were revealed by fluorescent tubulins and fluorescent EB1 simultaneously.

claim: Only a few resorbing MTs were captured in cells resuspended in 7.5 mM HA.
source: Only a few resorbing MTs were captured in cells resuspended in 7.5 mM HA (Figure 3a, right panel).

claim: All MT patterns and comets disappeared in cells resuspended in 10 mM HA.
source: All MT patterns and comets disappeared in cells resuspended in 10 mM HA.

claim: Low [HA] increases EB1 shank-binding, rendering the bird-cage pattern.
source: Therefore, low [HA] increases EB1 shank-binding, rendering the bird-cage pattern.

claim: As HA concentrations increase, MTs stop growing and comets are lost.
source: As HA concentrations increase, MTs stop growing and comets are lost.

claim: tub2 is a β-tubulin mutant with a missense mutation that results in more stable MTs.
source: Independently, we took a genetic approach, testing a tubulin mutant, tub2, hypothesizing that HA-elicited resorption would decelerate due to the more stable MTs resulted from a missense mutation in β-tubulin (Schibler and Huang, 1991).

claim: In EB1-NG transgenic tub2 cells, the comet pattern appeared indistinguishable from that in WT transgenic cells.
source: In the EB1-NG transgenic tub2 cells, the comet pattern (Figure 3b, top panels) appeared indistinguishable from that in WT transgenic cells (Figure 1b).

claim: In the image taken immediately after resuspension in 10 mM HA, the bird cage pattern with a few comet-like spots already formed in every tub2 cell.
source: Interestingly though, in the image taken immediately after resuspension in 10 mM HA, the bird cage pattern with a few comet-like spots already formed in every tub2 cell (bottom panels).

claim: The bird cage pattern in tub2 cells was rather stable after 10 mM HA exposure.
source: The pattern was rather stable, although some MTs seemed to be out of focus intermittently (bottom right panel), suggesting detachment from the plasma membrane.

claim: HA-induced diminished EB1-NG signals in WT cells are not due to reduced brightness of NG at low pH.
source: Thus, HA-induced diminished EB1-NG signals in WT cells are not due to reduced brightness of NG at low pH (Shaner et al., 2013).
evidence: Inference from tub2 results with citation

claim: In ~5 mM HA, dissociation of EB1 from MT plus ends is inhibited, leading to a bird cage like pattern.
source: Collectively, these data show that, in ~5 mM HA, dissociation of EB1 from MT plus ends is inhibited, leading to a bird cage like pattern.

claim: More concentrated HA blocks MT elongation while accelerates MT depolymerization.
source: More concentrated HA blocks MT elongation while accelerates MT depolymerization, which is prohibited by increased MT stability in tub2 cells.
evidence: Inference from concentration-dependent and mutant experiments

claim: Chelation of Ca2+ by pretreatment of cells with buffered 10 mM EGTA did not hinder HA-induced changes.
source: Chelation of Ca2+ by pretreatment of cells with buffered 10 mM EGTA did not hinder these changes, whereas pH3, 10 mM HCl did not elicit any responses.

claim: pH3, 10 mM HCl did not elicit any responses.
source: Chelation of Ca2+ by pretreatment of cells with buffered 10 mM EGTA did not hinder these changes, whereas pH3, 10 mM HCl did not elicit any responses.

claim: HA-elicited changes in cortical MTs are due to intracellular rather than extracellular acidification.
source: The simplest interpretation is that, as with deflagellation, HA-elicited changes in cortical MTs are due to intracellular rather than extracellular acidification; however, the changes do not require extracellular Ca2+.

claim: HA-elicited changes in cortical MTs do not require extracellular Ca2+.
source: The simplest interpretation is that, as with deflagellation, HA-elicited changes in cortical MTs are due to intracellular rather than extracellular acidification; however, the changes do not require extracellular Ca2+.

claim: Chlamydomonas expresses Na+/H+ exchangers.
source: Chlamydomonas expresses Na+/H+ exchangers (Pittman et al., 2009), as well as various channels and pumps for different locations (Fujiu et al., 2011; Taylor et al., 2012) to maintain electrolyte homeostasis.

claim: Chlamydomonas expresses various channels and pumps for different locations to maintain electrolyte homeostasis.
source: Chlamydomonas expresses Na+/H+ exchangers (Pittman et al., 2009), as well as various channels and pumps for different locations (Fujiu et al., 2011; Taylor et al., 2012) to maintain electrolyte homeostasis.

claim: EB1 patterns were absent except for the static signal at the BB area in cells resuspending in pH3, 10 mM HA/ddw for 5 min.
source: As expected, EB1 patterns were absent except for the static signal at the BB area in cells resuspending in pH3, 10 mM HA/double distilled water (ddw) for 5 min (Figure 4a, left panel).

claim: After wash with Na+/HEPES in a perfusion chamber, dynamic EB1 signals emerged at the BB area after ~50 s.
source: After wash with Na+/HEPES in a perfusion chamber, dynamic EB1 signals emerged at the BB area after ~50 s (Figure 4a, cell I in right panel).

claim: Nascent MTs after HA bath and Na+ wash were not adorned with a typical comet.
source: Interestingly, nascent MTs were not adorned with a typical comet.

claim: Nascent MTs after HA bath and Na+ wash appeared thicker, fewer and nearly uniformly decorated, as if plus end tracking EB1 stayed behind growing MTs.
source: Compared to the bird cage pattern, they appeared thicker, fewer and nearly uniformly decorated, as if plus end tracking EB1 stayed behind growing MTs.

claim: In cells recorded at a later period (between 60–159 s), MT growth decelerated, especially between 109–159 s.
source: In cells recorded at a later period (cell II and III, between 60–159 s; Video 5), MT growth decelerated, especially between 109–159 s.

claim: In the recordings started 180 s after wash, all dynamic processes stopped.
source: In the recordings started 180 s after wash, all dynamic processes stopped (Figure 4b, left panel), as illustrated by two nearly identical images taken 20 s apart of two representative cells (cell I and II, right panels).

claim: Some static fibers split, or had more than one comet aligned in tandem after HA bath and Na+ wash.
source: Notably, some static fibers split, or had more than one comet aligned in tandem (arrowheads).

claim: Nascent MTs generated after HA bath and wash are abnormal, perhaps with a propensity to nucleate ectopically, branching or growing on top of the other piggy-backing as bundles.
source: Taken together, these observations strongly suggest that nascent MTs generated after HA bath and wash are abnormal, perhaps with a propensity to nucleate ectopically, branching or growing on top of the other piggy-backing as bundles.

claim: EB1 signals reach near the BB area in cells recovering from HA bath.
source: Kymographs comparing three representative MTs (Figure 4c, top panels) with growing MTs in the untreated control cells (bottom panels) confirm that EB1 signals reach near the BB area in cells recovering from HA bath.

claim: MT growth rates fluctuate but are mostly slower than those in untreated control cells after HA bath and wash.
source: MT growth rates, shown by the slopes, fluctuate but are mostly slower than those in untreated control cells.

claim: Overall the MT growth rates decline until MT growth stops after HA bath and wash.
source: Overall the rates decline until MT growth stops.

claim: MTs formed in the recovery phase after HA bath were fewer, thicker, shorter, brighter and long-lived compared to the transient bird cage pattern.
source: Thus, compared to the numerous, thin, dim MT fibers in the transient bird cage pattern (Figure 3a), MTs formed in the recovery phase after HA bath were fewer, thicker, shorter, brighter and long-lived.

claim: The thick static MTs formed after HA bath and wash are cold stable.
source: As shown in two representative cells, EB1-decorated MTs after HA bath and wash remained after the removal from ice amidst the drift of focal planes (Figure 4d, top panels). Thus, the thick static MTs formed after HA bath and wash are cold stable.
evidence: Shown in Figure 4d cold treatment experiment

claim: For the control without HA bath, EB1 patterns were undetectable initially after cold treatment, indicating cold lability.
source: In contrast, for the control without HA bath, EB1 patterns were undetectable initially (bottom panels), indicating cold lability.

claim: Dynamic EB1 signals gradually re-emerged at BBs after 30 s in control cells after cold treatment.
source: Dynamic EB1 signals gradually re-emerged at BBs after 30 s (white arrowheads).

claim: Comet activity was vibrant in cells 55 mins post wash after HA bath.
source: Comet (Figure 4e, white arrowheads) activity was vibrant in cells 55 mins post wash, as if the freeze had never occurred.

claim: The frozen bird cage pattern remained in tub2 cells after 5 min HA bath.
source: As expected, the frozen bird cage pattern remained after 5 min HA bath (Figure 5a; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: After wash, comets returned and lengthened in tub2 cells as in WT cells.
source: After wash, comets returned (panel I and II) and lengthened as in WT cells.

claim: Comets appeared at the plus end of existing MTs first rather than at BBs in tub2 cells after HA bath and wash.
source: However, comets (white arrowheads) appeared at the plus end of existing MTs first rather than at BBs where nascent MTs emerged in WT cells (Figure 4a).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5a with comparison to WT

claim: The bird cage pattern gradually faded concomitantly with comet return in tub2 cells.
source: The bird cage pattern gradually faded concomitantly.

claim: 10 mM HA cannot elicit the resorption of the more stable MTs in tub2.
source: These collective results from tub2 indicate that 10 mM HA cannot elicit the resorption of the more stable MTs in tub2, as such the bird cage pattern with cortical MTs uniformly decorated with EB1 persists; the other reactions are similar in tub2 and WT cells recovering from HA bath, but comets preferentially return to old MTs, which need to resorb to make room for new ones to maintain the number of cortical MTs.

claim: Comets preferentially return to old MTs in tub2 cells, which need to resorb to make room for new ones to maintain the number of cortical MTs.
source: These collective results from tub2 indicate that 10 mM HA cannot elicit the resorption of the more stable MTs in tub2, as such the bird cage pattern with cortical MTs uniformly decorated with EB1 persists; the other reactions are similar in tub2 and WT cells recovering from HA bath, but comets preferentially return to old MTs, which need to resorb to make room for new ones to maintain the number of cortical MTs.

claim: EB1-decorated MT fibers formed only if the wash solution contained Na+, such as the NaOH-buffered HEPES (5 mM Na+) or 5 mM NaCl in ddw.
source: Interestingly, as shown by time-lapse images separated by a 10 s interval, EB1-decorated MT fibers formed only if the wash solution contained Na+, such as the NaOH-buffered HEPES (5 mM Na+) or 5 mM NaCl in ddw (Figure 6a, top two panels).

claim: Comets resumed profusely if the wash solution lacked Na+, such as the KOH-buffered HEPES buffer, 5 mM KCl in ddw or plain ddw.
source: On the other hand, comets resumed profusely if the wash solution lacked Na+, such as the KOH-buffered HEPES buffer, 5 mM KCl in ddw or plain ddw (bottom three panels).

claim: Na+ accounts for the reformation of thick, long-lived static MTs in the recovery phase of HA-bathed cells.
source: Therefore, Na+ accounts for the reformation of thick, long-lived static MTs in the recovery phase of HA-bathed cells.

claim: Thick MTs formed in cells resuspended in 21 mM Na+/EGTA for 5 min or 10 min.
source: MTs in cells were largely frozen after 5 min 10 mM pH3 HA bath and 3 min in the wash solution, such as 5 mM pH7.4 Na+/HEPES buffer or 5 mM NaCl solution (black arrowheads).

claim: Thick MTs were still growing after 5 min incubation in Na+/EGTA but static after 10 min incubation.
source: Thick MTs were still growing after 5 min incubation but static after 10 min incubation.

claim: Cells in 21 mM K+/EGTA had vibrant comet activities.
source: In contrast, cells resuspended in KOH-buffered EGTA had vibrant comet activities (right panels).

claim: Cells in K+/EGTA quickly burst, indicating the perturbed plasma membrane.
source: However, cells quickly burst, indicating the perturbed plasma membrane.

claim: In HEPES with 55 mM NaCl, MTs were still growing but with longer comets.
source: Compared to the growing MTs with typical comets in control cells resuspended in the HEPES buffer, in HEPES with 55 mM NaCl, MTs were still growing but with longer comets as shown in fluorescent imaging (Figure 6c panel I) and modest tapering of comet intensity in the linescan plot (panel II).

claim: The average velocity of comets at 55 mM Na+ was significantly different from 5 mM Na+ (two-tailed p-value=0.0497, <0.05).
source: The distribution of comet velocity (panel III) and the average velocity (panel IV) showed that [Na+]in at this level only slightly reduced MT growth rate (two-tailed p-value=0.0497, <0.05).

claim: High [Na+]ex can raise [Na+]in, increasing the time EB1 spent at the plus end and thus comet lengths.
source: Therefore, high [Na+]ex still could raise [Na+]in, increasing the time EB1 spent at the plus end and thus comet lengths.

claim: MT growth is sensitive to [Na+] but less than EB1 plus end binding.
source: MT growth is also sensitive to [Na+] but less than EB1 plus end binding.

claim: For cells resuspended in 150 and 200 mM [Na+]ex for 5 min, flagellar motility ceased.
source: For cells resuspended in 150 and 200 mM [Na+]ex for 5 min, flagellar motility ceased.

claim: In most cells at 150-200 mM Na+, comets vanished, although static EB1 signals remained at the BB area.
source: In most cells, comets vanished, although static EB1 signals remained at the BB area (Figure 6d), as in 75 mM [Ca2+] solution (Figure 2g).

claim: The algal MT system undergoes a range of changes as a function of [Na+].
source: Together, these results show that the MT system undergo a range of changes as a function of [Na+].

claim: Frozen thick MTs caused by 21 mM Na+/EGTA or by 5 mM Na+/HEPES wash following an HA bath may be triggered by less than 21 mM [Na+]in.
source: Frozen thick MTs caused by 21 mM Na+/EGTA or by 5 mM Na+/HEPES wash following an HA bath or may be triggered by less than 21 mM [Na+]in respectively due to passive diffusion through the EGTA-permeabilized membrane or by H+/Na+ exchange.

claim: [Na+]in is likely even lower in cells which are simply exposed to 55 mM [Na+]ex, and have long comets and growing MTs.
source: [Na+]in is likely even lower in cells which are simply exposed to 55 mM [Na+]ex, and have long comets and growing MTs.

claim: Few or no EB1-decorated thick MT fibers caused by 150–200 mM [Na+]ex or 75 mM [Ca2+]ex suggest that MTs disassemble at the concentrations that deem hypertonic for Chlamydomonas.
source: In contrary, few or no EB1-decorated thick MT fibers caused by 150–200 mM [Na+]ex or 75 mM [Ca2+]ex suggest that MTs disassemble at the concentrations that deem hypertonic for Chlamydomonas.

claim: Salt stress triggers an array of responses in Chlamydomonas, including inhibited multiplication.
source: Salt stress triggers an array of responses in Chlamydomonas, including inhibited multiplication (Perrineau et al., 2014; Takouridis et al., 2015).

claim: In typical synchronized liquid cultures, mother cells undergo 1–3 rounds of cell division during the dark period, each forming a sporangium with multiple daughter cells enclosed in the mother cell wall.
source: In typical synchronized liquid cultures, mother cells undergo 1–3 rounds of cell division during the dark period, each forming a sporangium with multiple daughter cells enclosed in the mother cell wall.
evidence: Description of normal cell division with citation

claim: Daughter cells are released before the light period.
source: Daughter cells are released before the light period (Kubo et al., 2009).

claim: Sporangia ratios were inversely related to NaCl concentrations.
source: Sporangia ratios were inversely related to NaCl concentrations (Figure 7a).

claim: The peak period of sporangia formation was delayed for 100 mM NaCl samples.
source: The peak period was also delayed for 100 mM samples.

claim: No sporangia were observed in 200 mM NaCl samples.
source: No sporangia were observed in 200 mM samples.

claim: No comets or EB1-decorated MTs were observed in 200 mM NaCl samples.
source: A repeated experiment for fluorescence imaging confirmed the trend, and showed no comets or EB1-decorated MTs in 200 mM samples (Figure 7b).

claim: Comets lengthened in 55 and 100 mM Na+/TAP.
source: As in 55 mM Na+/HEPES (Figure 6c), comets lengthened in 55 and 100 mM Na+/TAP, but a linescan plot (Figure 7c, left panel) showed that the lengthening degrees appeared similar.

claim: Mean comet speeds at 55 mM (8.38 ± 0.345 μm/min) and 100 mM (7.79 ± 0.628 μm/min) were not significantly different (two-tailed t test, p=0.385).
source: Mean comet speeds (right panel), 8.38 ± 0.345 μm/min and 7.79 ± 0.628 μm/min respectively for 55 and 100 mM samples, were not significantly different (two-tailed t test, p=0.385), but faster than 6.41 ± 0.241 μm/min for 0 mM samples (two-tailed t test, p<0.001 for 0 mM and 55 mM samples; Mann-Whitney U test, p=0.05 for 0 mM and 100 mM samples).

claim: Mean comet speeds at 55 mM and 100 mM were faster than 6.41 ± 0.241 μm/min for 0 mM samples.
source: Mean comet speeds (right panel), 8.38 ± 0.345 μm/min and 7.79 ± 0.628 μm/min respectively for 55 and 100 mM samples, were not significantly different (two-tailed t test, p=0.385), but faster than 6.41 ± 0.241 μm/min for 0 mM samples (two-tailed t test, p<0.001 for 0 mM and 55 mM samples; Mann-Whitney U test, p=0.05 for 0 mM and 100 mM samples).

claim: Absence of comets and decorated MTs is consistent with blocked proliferation of cells exposed to 200 mM NaCl.
source: Thus, absence of comets and decorated MTs is consistent with blocked proliferation of cells exposed to 200 mM NaCl.

claim: The similar comet lengths and comet speeds for the 55 and 100 mM NaCl group do not correlate with differences in the numbers of dividing cells and the delay.
source: However, the similar comet lengths and comet speeds for the 55 and 100 mM NaCl group do not correlate with differences in the numbers of dividing cells and the delay.

claim: The changes of algal MT system elicited by intracellular acidification are swift, stunning and novel.
source: The changes of algal MT system elicited by intracellular acidification are swift, stunning and novel (Figures 2b–e and 3).

claim: The bird cage pattern of shank binding is the most sensitive response, elicited reliably by 5 mM HA.
source: Among heightened shank binding, diminished comet activity, paused MT growths, and MT shortening, the bird cage pattern of shank binding is the most sensitive, elicited reliably by 5 mM HA (Figure 3a).

claim: Extracellular Ca2+ is not required for the HA-induced changes, since they still occur after K+/EGTA treatment.
source: Extracellular Ca2+ is not required for the HA-induced changes, since they still occur after K+/EGTA treatment.

claim: The intracellular pH resulting from [HA]ex that triggers these changes is expected to be higher than 6.3.
source: Although the pH of [HA]ex that triggers these changes is ~3.4, we expect that the resulting intracellular pH is higher than 6.3.

claim: HA-induced changes in diffusion chambers appear before deflagellation that occurs at pH6.3.
source: Firstly, HA-induced changes in diffusion chambers appear before deflagellation (Figure 2e) that occurs at pH6.3 (Wheeler et al., 2008; Braun and Hegemann, 1999).

claim: The swiftness and reversibility of HA-induced changes indicate that these changes are not triggered by apoptotic pathways.
source: Secondly, the swiftness and reversibility (Figures 2b, 3a, 4a and 5a) indicate that these changes are not triggered by apoptotic pathways, commonly induced by a drop of 0.3–0.4 unit from normal intracellular pH (Lagadic-Gossmann et al., 2004), which is 6.8 for Chlamydomonas (Wheeler et al., 2008).

claim: Normal intracellular pH is 6.8 for Chlamydomonas.
source: Secondly, the swiftness and reversibility (Figures 2b, 3a, 4a and 5a) indicate that these changes are not triggered by apoptotic pathways, commonly induced by a drop of 0.3–0.4 unit from normal intracellular pH (Lagadic-Gossmann et al., 2004), which is 6.8 for Chlamydomonas (Wheeler et al., 2008).

claim: A slight imbalance of pH homeostasis is sufficient to elicit immediate changes in algal MT system.
source: These observations strongly suggest that a slight imbalance of pH homeostasis is sufficient to elicit immediate changes in algal MT system.

claim: The respective pI of Chlamydomonas α-tubulin, β-tubulin and EB1 is 5.01, 4.82, and 5.7.
source: For example, the respective pI of Chlamydomonasα-tubulin, β-tubulin and EB1 is 5.01, 4.82, and 5.7.

claim: A decrease of pH from the resting level will make tubulins and EB1 less negatively charged, especially at their C-terminal acidic tails.
source: A decrease of pH from the resting level will make these proteins less negatively charged, especially at their C-terminal acidic tails that are central to MT-accessory protein interplays and the targets of various post-translational modifications (reviewed by Song and Brady, 2015; Buey et al., 2011; Rovini et al., 2013).
evidence: Inference based on chemistry with citations

claim: The resulting decreased repulsion could explain increased affinity of EB1 to GDP-tubulin, leading to the bird cage pattern.
source: The resulting decreased repulsion could explain increased affinity of EB1 to GDP-tubulin, leading to nearly immediate appearance of the bird cage pattern in WT cells exposed to 5 mM HA (Figure 3a) or in tub2 cells exposed to 10 mM HA (Figure 3b and 5a).

claim: As pH decreases further, additional changes in protein conformation may inhibit the growth of MTs and EB1 binding to plus ends, leading to comet reduction or ultimate disappearance.
source: As pH decreases further, additional changes in protein conformation may inhibit the growth of MTs and EB1 binding to plus ends, leading to comet reduction or ultimate disappearance.

claim: The responses elicited by slight increases in [Na+]in and [H+]in are distinct in pattern and pace.
source: The responses elicited by slight increases in [Na+]in and [H+]in are distinct in pattern and pace.

claim: The slower pace of low-Na+-induced responses are likely due to low Na+ permeability.
source: The slower pace of low-Na+-induced responses are likely due to low Na+ permeability.

claim: Na+ has low permeability compared to K+.
source: Since Na+ has low permeability compared to K+ (Ronkin and Buretz, 1960), we predict that Na+ ions from the wash buffer are entering the cytosol when Na+/H+ exchangers are removing H+.

claim: The direct switch from lengthening comets to MT resorption suggests that NaCl alone cannot raise [Na+]in incrementally.
source: The direct switch from lengthening comets to MT resorption (Figures 6c, 7b and c) suggests that NaCl alone cannot raise [Na+]in incrementally.

claim: Continual aggravated changes until MTs become static during a 10 min period in 21 mM Na+/EGTA indicate that they are occurring before [Na+]in reaches 21 mM.
source: Continual aggravated changes until MTs become static during a 10 min period in 21 mM Na+/EGTA (Figure 6b) indicate that they are occurring before [Na+]in reaches 21 mM, which is made possible by EGTA treatment.

claim: Similar Na+-dependent responses emerge faster following a HA bath – in 45–180 s in various wash solutions containing only 5 mM Na+, suggesting accelerated rise of [Na+]in due to the activity of Na+/ H+ exchangers.
source: Similar Na+-dependent responses emerge faster following a HA bath – in 45–180 s in various wash solutions containing only 5 mM Na+ (Figures 4a and 6a), suggesting accelerated rise of [Na+]in due to the activity of Na+/ H+ exchangers to remove accumulated H+ ions (Pittman et al., 2009).

claim: Algal MT system changes as a function of [Na+]in based on the incremented responses, rather than all-or-none responses to a threshold.
source: Based on the incremented responses, rather than all-or-none responses to a threshold, we speculate that algal MT system changes as a function of [Na+]in.

claim: Raising [K+]ex had no evident effect on the MT system, contrary to [Na+]ex.
source: Contrary to [Na+]ex, raising [K+]ex had no evident effect (Figure 6a).

claim: [K+]in is ~70 mM in Chlamydomonas cells.
source: This is reasonable, given high [K+]in, ~70 mM in Chlamydomonas cells (Malhotra and Glass, 1995).

claim: The selective sensitivity of the algal MT system to Na+ rules out mere ionic effects.
source: This highlights the selective sensitivity of the algal MT system to Na+ and rules out mere ionic effects.

claim: One possibility is that Na+ binds to particular sites in algal tubulins, analogous to Ca2+ binding sites in mammalian tubulins.
source: One interesting possibility is that Na+ binds to particular sites in algal tubulins, analogous to Ca2+ binding sites in mammalian tubulins (Solomon, 1977; Serrano et al., 1986).

claim: EB1 signals largely vanish at or above 150 mM [Na+]ex, as in 10 mM HA and 75 mM [Ca2+]ex except residual static signals at the BB area.
source: EB1 signals largely vanish at or above 150 mM [Na+]ex (Figures 6d and 7b), as in 10 mM HA (Figures 2c and 4a) and 75 mM [Ca2+]ex (Figure 2g) except residual static signals at the BB area.

claim: These changes likely reflect simultaneous disassembly and paused new growth, and an immobile EB1 population underneath BBs respectively.
source: These changes likely reflect simultaneous disassembly and paused new growth, and an immobile EB1 population underneath BBs respectively (Yan et al., 2006; Pedersen et al., 2003).

claim: The similar outcomes caused by distinct ions and obvious shrinkage of the cell body at even higher concentrations of Na+ and Ca2+ suggest that hypertonicity is involved.
source: The similar outcomes caused by distinct ions and obvious shrinkage of the cell body at even higher concentrations of Na+ and Ca2+ suggest that hypertonicity is involved.

claim: High concentration responses could be caused by one cation exceeding a threshold concentration; or concurrent rises of multiple electrolytes as H2O moves out of cells.
source: We envisage that high concentration responses could be caused by one cation exceeding a threshold concentration; or concurrent rises of multiple electrolytes as H2O moves out of cells.

claim: The capture of endwise resorption only in low concentration conditions suggests that increased concentrations of these ions heighten shortening- the incidence and/or speed.
source: The capture of endwise resorption only in low concentration conditions (Figures 2d and 3a) suggests that increased concentrations of these ions heighten shortening- the incidence and/or speed.

claim: 0.5–0.6 mM Ca2+ - in the absence of MAPs - could increase shortening incidence and accelerate shortening speed of MTs beyond 150 μm/min.
source: Ca2+ blocks MT formation (Weisenberg, 1972), whereas 0.5–0.6 mM Ca2+ - in the absence of MAPs - could increase shortening incidence and accelerate shortening speed of MTs beyond 150 μm/min (Karr et al., 1980; O'Brien et al., 1997).

claim: pH shock and high [Ca2+]ex only temporarily raise [Ca2+]in up to 1 μM.
source: Although pH shock and high [Ca2+]ex only temporarily raise [Ca2+]in up to 1 μM (Wheeler et al., 2008), the lower concentration may be sufficient to accelerate shortening.

claim: Some electrolyte-elicited changes could be evoked by signaling pathways in Chlamydomonas, which perhaps occur later and slower; and last longer than the direct effects from electrolytes.
source: Some electrolyte-elicited changes could be evoked by signaling pathways in Chlamydomonas as in other organisms (Wang et al., 2013; Perrineau et al., 2014; Khona et al., 2016), which perhaps occur later and slower; and last longer than the direct effects from electrolytes.

claim: Kinesin-13 becomes phosphorylated for more than 20 min following pH shock to catalyze MT endwise disassembly to provide tubulins for flagellar regeneration.
source: For example, kinesin-13 becomes phosphorylated for more than 20 min following pH shock to catalyze MT endwise disassembly to provide tubulins for flagellar regeneration (Wang et al., 2013).

claim: Osmotic or salt stresses activate an atypical tubulin-kinase and phospholipase D, triggering disassembly or reorganization of plant MT system.
source: Similarly, osmotic or salt stresses activate an atypical tubulin-kinase and phospholipase D, triggering disassembly or reorganization of plant MT system (Fujita et al., 2013; Dhonukshe et al., 2003).

claim: For yeast, sorbitol hypertonicity induces frozen MTs.
source: For yeast, sorbitol hypertonicity induces frozen MTs (Robertson and Hagan, 2008) and the recovery in 38 min involves a stress-induced MAP kinase.

claim: The electrolyte sensitivity of algal MT system is contrary to the perceived stable MT system in interphase mammalian cells.
source: The electrolyte sensitivity of algal MT system is contrary to the perceived stable MT system in interphase mammalian cells (Lieuvin et al., 1994) that have 140 mM [Na+]ex, and 140 mM [K+]in (reviewed by Pohl et al., 2013).

claim: Mammalian cells have 140 mM [Na+]ex, and 140 mM [K+]in.
source: The electrolyte sensitivity of algal MT system is contrary to the perceived stable MT system in interphase mammalian cells (Lieuvin et al., 1994) that have 140 mM [Na+]ex, and 140 mM [K+]in (reviewed by Pohl et al., 2013).

claim: Compression or illumination cannot elicit any obvious changes of EB1-EGFP patterns in mammalian epithelial cells.
source: Consistent with this, we cannot elicit any obvious changes of EB1-EGFP patterns in mammalian epithelial cells by compression or illumination (Matov et al., 2010).

claim: Both Na+ and K+ promote tubulin polymerization, with 160 mM Na+ as the optimal condition.
source: Likewise, both Na+ and K+ promote tubulin polymerization, with 160 mM Na+ as the optimal condition (Olmsted and Borisy, 1975).

claim: Different cation sensitivities could be due to sequence divergence.
source: Different cation sensitivities could be due to sequence divergence.

claim: The presence of accessory proteins, such as MAPs may obscure the cation sensitivity of mammalian MTs.
source: The other possible cause is the presence of accessory proteins, such as MAPs that obscure the cation sensitivity of mammalian MTs (Olmsted and Borisy, 1975; Wolff et al., 1996).

claim: While fundamental features of the MT system - likely dynamic instability and EB1 plus end tracking - are universal, electrolyte sensitivity and responses could diverge.
source: Thus, while fundamental features of the MT system - likely dynamic instability and EB1 plus end tracking - are universal, electrolyte sensitivity and responses could diverge.

claim: The pH gradient at the pollen tube may account for the establishment of the MT zone lagging the F-actin, Ca2+ and acid zone at the very tip.
source: For example, the pH gradient at the pollen tube may account for the establishment of the MT zone lagging the F-actin, Ca2+ and acid zone at the very tip (Gibbon and Kropf, 1994; reviewed by Hepler, 2016).

claim: For sea urchins, a basic shift directs MT-supported processes following fertilization.
source: For sea urchins, a basic shift directs MT-supported processes following fertilization.

claim: Depressing pH triggers MT disassembly and inhibits division of fertilized zygotes in sea urchins.
source: Depressing pH triggers MT disassembly and inhibits division of fertilized zygotes (Schatten et al., 1985).

claim: An increase of 0.3–0.5 pH unit occurs in mitosis.
source: This and an increase of 0.3–0.5 pH unit in mitosis inspired the pH clock hypothesis for cell cycle control (Gagliardi and Shain, 2013).

claim: EB1 preferentially binds to MT plus ends in arrested mitotic phase extract of Xenopus oocytes, but uniformly decorates MTs in interphase extract.
source: In line with this, EB1 preferentially binds to MT plus ends in arrested mitotic phase extract of Xenopus oocytes, but uniformly decorates MTs in interphase extract (Tirnauer et al., 2002), perhaps with a lower pH, analogous to HA-induced bird cage pattern (Figure 3a).

claim: Tuning pH may control cell cycle for certain organisms given the central roles of EB1 and dynamic MTs for mitosis and the swiftness of pH-induced changes.
source: Given the central roles of EB1 and dynamic MTs for mitosis and the swiftness of pH-induced changes in MTs and EB1 patterns, tuning pH may indeed control cell cycle for certain organisms.

claim: Absence of most EB1 signals correlates with blocked cell division at 200 mM NaCl.
source: Similarly, absence of most EB1 signals correlates with blocked cell division at 200 mM NaCl (Figure 7).

claim: Proliferation of commonly used Chlamydomonas strains is mostly blocked in the culture media containing NaCl of 200 mM or a higher concentration.
source: Consistent with this, proliferation of commonly used Chlamydomonas strains is mostly blocked in the culture media containing NaCl of 200 mM or a higher concentraion (Perrineau et al., 2014; Takouridis et al., 2015; Khona et al., 2016) in the efforts of industrial scale cultures of microalgae with media of high salinity.

claim: Adaptation to high salinity takes months and involves mutation, sexual reproduction and evolution.
source: Adaptation to such salinity takes months and involves mutation, sextual reproduction and evolution.

claim: The MT system is likely one of the limiting factors for proliferation at high salinity.
source: The MT system is likely one of the limiting factors.

claim: Proliferation is also partially inhibited at 55 and 100 mM NaCl at least within 24 hr.
source: This study also shows that proliferation is also partially inhibited at 55 and100 mM at least within 24 hr.

claim: Cell division at ~100 mM NaCl may be inhibited by additional reactions that may or may not relate to the MT system.
source: Perhaps cell division at ~100 mM NaCl is inhibited by additional reactions that may or may not relate to the MT system.

claim: Intracellular acidification followed by immersions in buffers with merely 5 mM Na+ may mimic changes in natural environments.
source: Intracellular acidification followed by immersions in buffers with merely 5 mM Na+ (Figure 6a) may mimick changes in natural environments.

claim: Acidity and salinity are key factors affecting the biota.
source: Acidity and salinity are key factors affecting the biota.

claim: Acidity and salinity vary drastically, often seasonally, among freshwater ecosystems, influenced by a combination of climate changes, biogeochemistry, episodic storm surges, snow melts and anthropological activities.
source: They vary drastically, often seasonally, among freshwater ecosystems, influenced by a combination of climate changes, biogeochemistry, episodic storm surges, snow melts and anthropological activities (reviewed by Sullivan, 2000; Herbert et al., 2015).

claim: pH following a downpour could decrease by one pH unit and to ~4.5 for typical watersheds.
source: Notably, pH following a downpour could decrease by one pH unit and to ~4.5 for typical watersheds (Feeley et al., 2013).

claim: Dissolved organic carbons, such as permeant HA, are a major contributor to local acidification, reaching up to mM levels.
source: Dissolved organic carbons, such as permeant HA, are a major contributor to local acidification, reaching up to mM levels (Monteith et al., 2007; Porcal et al., 2009; Zuo et al., 2012).

claim: Acidification caused by acid rains from air pollution occurred primarily in the past.
source: In addition, acidification caused by acid rains from air pollution primarily in the past (Sullivan, 2000) and by the projected increase in atmospheric CO2 in the future (Raven and Caldeira, 2005) will also shift the equilibrium toward permeant neutral acids and favor intracellular acidification.

claim: The projected increase in atmospheric CO2 in the future will shift the equilibrium toward permeant neutral acids and favor intracellular acidification.
source: In addition, acidification caused by acid rains from air pollution primarily in the past (Sullivan, 2000) and by the projected increase in atmospheric CO2 in the future (Raven and Caldeira, 2005) will also shift the equilibrium toward permeant neutral acids and favor intracellular acidification.

claim: Salinity-dependent effects on Chlamydomonas typify the inverse relationship of salinity and species diversity.
source: Salinity-dependent effects on Chlamydomonas (Figure 7a) typify the inverse relationship of salinity and species diversity; and the exceptional vulnerability to salinity of microalgae and zooplanktons that are at the bottom of the food chain (reviewed by Herbert et al., 2015).

claim: Microalgae and zooplanktons are exceptionally vulnerable to salinity and are at the bottom of the food chain.
source: Salinity-dependent effects on Chlamydomonas (Figure 7a) typify the inverse relationship of salinity and species diversity; and the exceptional vulnerability to salinity of microalgae and zooplanktons that are at the bottom of the food chain (reviewed by Herbert et al., 2015).

claim: The sub- or hypo-saline level of 55 mM Na+ that perturbs alga's MT system and cell division is readily exceeded by Na+ concentration in numerous inland and coastal wetlands throughout the world.
source: The sub- or hypo-saline level of 55 mM Na+ that perturbs alga's MT system and cell division is readily exceeded by Na+ concentration in numerous inland and coastal wetlands throughout the world from intrusion of seawater (~469 mM Na+), rising of saline ground water and mining effluent discharges (Herbert et al., 2015).

claim: Seawater contains ~469 mM Na+.
source: The sub- or hypo-saline level of 55 mM Na+ that perturbs alga's MT system and cell division is readily exceeded by Na+ concentration in numerous inland and coastal wetlands throughout the world from intrusion of seawater (~469 mM Na+), rising of saline ground water and mining effluent discharges (Herbert et al., 2015).

claim: Deicing road salt for traffic safety is transforming pristine water bodies in North America, especially urban riverways.
source: Similarly, deicing road salt for traffic safety is transforming pristine water bodies in North America, especially urban riverways (Corsi et al., 2010; Dugan et al., 2017; Jones et al., 2017).

claim: Cl- exceeded 24 mM (860 mg/L), the acute criteria for aquatic life established by United States Environmental Protection Agency, in more than 55% of tested sites at the Milwaukee river basin.
source: For example, Cl-, a standard salinity indicator, exceeded 24 mM (860 mg/L), the acute criteria for aquatic life established by United States Environmental Protection Agency, in more than 55% of tested sites at the Milwaukee river basin, a major estuary of the Great Lakes, and was as high as 315 mM (Corsi et al., 2010).

claim: Cl- was as high as 315 mM at the Milwaukee river basin.
source: For example, Cl-, a standard salinity indicator, exceeded 24 mM (860 mg/L), the acute criteria for aquatic life established by United States Environmental Protection Agency, in more than 55% of tested sites at the Milwaukee river basin, a major estuary of the Great Lakes, and was as high as 315 mM (Corsi et al., 2010).

claim: Current concerns about rising atmospheric CO2 largely center on extracellular acidification and hindered shell formation.
source: While current concerns about rising atmospheric CO2 largely center on extracellular acidification and hindered shell formation (Hoegh-Guldberg et al., 2007; Waldbusser et al., 2013; Fitzer et al., 2016), this study suggests that the concerns should be extended to intracellular acidification, rising salinity and the MT system.

claim: Concerns about rising atmospheric CO2 should be extended to intracellular acidification, rising salinity and the MT system.
source: While current concerns about rising atmospheric CO2 largely center on extracellular acidification and hindered shell formation (Hoegh-Guldberg et al., 2007; Waldbusser et al., 2013; Fitzer et al., 2016), this study suggests that the concerns should be extended to intracellular acidification, rising salinity and the MT system.

claim: Seemingly harmless rises in salinity in conjunction with chronic mild acidification or a temporary acid surge may threaten vulnerable unicellular organisms via a perturbed MT system.
source: Seemingly harmless rises in salinity in conjunction with chronic mild acidification or a temporary acid surge may poise to threaten the vulnerable unicellular organisms via a perturbed MT system, reshape aqueous landscapes and drive evolution.

claim: Electrolyte-induced rapid changes in the MT system may be applicable to land plants and even particular mammalian cells.
source: Electrolyte-induced rapid changes in the MT system may be applicable to land plants and even particular mammalian cells.

claim: Land plant model systems subjected to salt stress, osmostress, or biotic stresses exhibit growth inhibition, MT bundling and heightened sensitivity to microtubule-stabilizing Taxol.
source: Like Chlamydomonas, land plant model systems subjected to salt stress, osmostress, or biotic stresses exhibit growth inhibition, MT bundling and heightened sensitivity to microtubule-stabilizing Taxol (e.g. Dhonukshe et al., 2003; Shoji et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2012; Fujita et al., 2013; reviewed by Hardam, 2013; Hashimoto, 2015; Oda, 2015).

claim: The similarity between Chlamydomonas and land plants comports with their common cortical MTs and a great homology of the non-flagellar proteins in the MT system.
source: The similarity comports with their common cortical MTs and a great homology of the non-flagellar proteins in the MT system (Dymek et al., 2006; Pedersen et al., 2003; Merchant et al., 2007; reviewe by Gardiner, 2013).

claim: MT changes induced by various abiotic stresses, including salt, have prompted a proposition that the MT system is an abiotic sensor of plant cells.
source: MT changes induced by various abiotic stresses, including salt, have prompted an interesting proposition that the MT system is an abiotic sensor of plant cells (Haswell and Verslues, 2015; Wang et al., 2011a, 2011b).

claim: The EB1-reported scaled responses that seem proportional to [Na+]in and the speed of manifestations in fresh water algae strengthen the possibility that plant MT system is an upstream player in the salinity signaling pathways, if not the very sensor.
source: The EB1-reported scaled responses that seem proportional to [Na+]in and the speed of manifestations (Figures 4d and 5) in fresh water algae strengthen the possibility that plant MT system is an upstream player in the salinity signaling pathways, if not the very sensor.

claim: Channel-linked MTs are integral to osmolarity signaling transduction in mammalian osmosensory neurons.
source: In line with this, channel-linked MTs are integral to osmolarity signaling transduction in mammalian osmosensory neurons (Prager-Khoutorsky et al., 2014).

claim: The wild type strain used is CC-124.
source: The wild type strain CC-124 and a β-tubulin mutant tub2-1 (formerly colR4) (Bolduc et al., 1988; Lee, 1990; Schibler and Huang, 1991) were from Chlamydomonas Resource Center (http://www.chlamycollection.org/).

claim: tub2-1 (formerly colR4) is a β-tubulin mutant.
source: The wild type strain CC-124 and a β-tubulin mutant tub2-1 (formerly colR4) (Bolduc et al., 1988; Lee, 1990; Schibler and Huang, 1991) were from Chlamydomonas Resource Center (http://www.chlamycollection.org/).

claim: Cells were cultured in 300 ml pH7.0 standard Tris Acetate Phosphate (TAP) liquid media with aeration at 25°C over a 14/10 light/dark cycle until reaching logarithmic phase of growth (5–10 × 10^6 cells/ml).
source: Cells were cultured in 300 ml pH7.0 standard Tris Aacetate Phosphate (TAP) liquid media with aeration at 25°C over a 14/10 light/dark cycle until reaching logarithmic phase of growth (5–10 × 106 cells/ml) (Sivadas et al., 2012).

claim: All experiments were completed at least 2 hr before the onset of the dark period.
source: All experiments were completed at least 2 hr before the onset of the dark period.

claim: EB1-NG in live Chlamydomonas cells was imaged with Nikon Eclipse widefield microscope equipped with a short-arc mercury lamp, an FITC-HYQ optical filter set, a CoolSNAP-ES CCD camera and MetaMorph software.
source: EB1-NG in live Chlamydomonas cells was imaged with Nikon Eclipse widefield microscope equipped with a short-arc mercury lamp, an FITC-HYQ optical filter set, a CoolSNAP-ES CCD camera and MetaMorph software.

claim: Each image was captured as a 16-bit grayscale file with 1 s exposure.
source: Each image was captured as a 16-bit grayscale file with 1 s exposure.

claim: Streaming videos were recorded for 100 frames at a rate of 1 frame/sec.
source: Streaming videos were recorded for 100 frames at a rate of 1 frame/sec.
